segments.title: Chương 89: 0089 【Tự do đến thái quá】
segments.content:
The next day, Chen Guiliang went to handle his enrollment procedures, but it wasn't time for the military training physical examination yet.

At noon, he ate at Peking University's No. 1 Cafeteria, which was very close to his dormitory. At the cafeteria entrance stood two old pagoda trees, rumored to be from the grand entrance of the late Qing Dynasty's Grand Council.

Rumors are generally unreliable.

Jiang Junlai heard that Zhongguancun was right next door, so he dragged Chen Guiliang there to look around.

"Wow, that's Lenovo!"

"Look on the wall of that building, it's got Baidu's paw print logo. Baidu must be in there."

"Sohu! Sohu!"

"And Sina! Damn, damn. Let me see if I can find NetEase..."

Jiang Junlai was acting like he'd gone mad, letting out exclamations of surprise from time to time.

Chen Guiliang, however, was taking the opportunity to familiarize himself with the streets. He wanted to start his own company. He certainly wouldn't have a physical office address, so he'd have to pay to register it under some other unit.

For this kind of thing, he would have to ask the senior students.

The Yuanpei Program was treated like a stepchild, so it was natural for its students to band together for warmth, especially since communication between different class years was extremely smooth.

Those senior students were scattered across all the university's various departments. They were doing all sorts of things, so getting information from them was very convenient. Usually, a barbecue meal was all it took to get things done.

Long Xiang sent a text: "Class meeting tonight at 7:30, Second Classroom Building, Room 101. Bring your roommate."

"Got it," Chen Guiliang replied.

They wandered around Zhongguancun until after five in the afternoon before Chen Guiliang and Jiang Junlai strolled back to campus for dinner.

To be honest, the food at the No. 1 Cafeteria wasn't that great.

Especially for southern students accustomed to rice, the rice at No. 1 Cafeteria didn't even pass muster. The grains were distinct and so hard they hurt your teeth!

But the dishes were quite heavy on oil and salt, which suited a heavy-flavor person like Chen Guiliang.

The upside was that it was cheap.

The most expensive braised pork was 3 yuan a serving, the cheapest stir-fried cabbage was 5 jiao a serving, and there was free seaweed and egg drop soup.

For those exceptionally frugal students, a meal of cabbage and rice could cost just one yuan.

"The rice is so bad."

Jiang Junlai said in a low voice, afraid of being overheard.

Chen Guiliang lamented, "Looks like we'll have to change our staple food. I saw the noodle dishes look pretty good."

Jiang Junlai said, "Eating noodles once in a while is okay, but we can't have steamed buns and noodles for every single meal, can we?"

Chen Guiliang was inexplicably reminded of Xie Yang. That guy had run off to study in Hangzhou, and his food situation was even more miserable than his own.

Xu Haibo had it the most comfortable, choosing to stay in Sichuan.

"Let's try a different cafeteria tomorrow," Chen Guiliang said, frustrated. "I refuse to believe every single cafeteria at Peking University can make rice this horrible."

Jiang Junlai asked, "What if they're all like this?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Then all I can do is admire the chefs at Peking University."

Complaining about the cafeteria rice all the way, the two returned to their dorm in Building 36 to rest, waiting until it was time to head to the large classroom in the Second Classroom Building.

Just as they were leaving, two people emerged from Room 403 across the hall. They were also freshmen from the Yuanpei Program.

Chen Guiliang greeted them proactively, and they all exchanged names and where they were from.

One was named Yun Fan, the provincial top scorer in liberal arts.

The other was Deng Chen, fourth place in the provincial science stream and the city's top scorer.

"Holy crap, you're Chen Guiliang!"

Deng Chen exclaimed in a Sichuan dialect: "A fellow provincial! I'm from the city right next to yours."

"What a coincidence. We can go home together for holidays in the future," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Yun Fan, the liberal arts top scorer from his province, had never heard of Chen Guiliang. He asked his roommate Deng Chen, "Is Chen Guiliang famous?"

"He's super famous, especially back in Sichuan," Deng Chen said in surprise. "You're a liberal arts student, how could you not know him?"

Yun Fan smiled shyly.

The four of them went downstairs together and ran into two more freshmen who, upon asking, turned out to be from the History Department.

Chen Guiliang asked a few more people along the way; they were either from the History Department or the Chinese Department. It seemed Building 36 was the dormitory for the History and Chinese departments, and the Yuanpei students were the ones just lodging here.

Chen Guiliang glanced at the girls' floors. If the freshmen from the Chinese Department were all here, it was highly likely he was living in the same dormitory building as Wu Meng.

"You're Chen Guiliang?" another freshman from the Chinese Department asked in pleasant surprise.

Chen Guiliang responded with a smile.

Yun Fan grew more and more puzzled: Is Chen Guiliang that famous? Why do so many people know him?

When they arrived at Room 101 of the Second Classroom Building, over a hundred people had already gathered.

The prime spots in the front and center had been mostly taken by students.

Chen Guiliang, Jiang Junlai, Yun Fan, and Deng Chen looked around and could only find seats in the second row.

About ten minutes later, all the students had finally arrived.

A teacher and 14 third-year students (counselors) also came.

The teacher walked up to the podium and said, "My name is Xiong Wenxin. I teach Chinese language and am not your head teacher, academic advisor, or counselor. The Yuanpei Program advocates for student autonomy. Once you elect a class committee, the committee will be responsible for everything!"

This statement caused a stir of astonishment among the crowd.

At the same time, it was novel. Student autonomy sounded very interesting.

Teacher Xiong Wenxin continued, "Of course, you've just entered university and are not familiar with anything yet. So, there are 14 third-year senior students to act as counselors to guide you. Each third-year counselor is responsible for 10 to 11 freshmen. The school doesn't manage the assignments; it will likely align with the academic advisor you choose."

Deng Chen clicked his tongue. "Such a high degree of freedom."

"It's a free-range model," Yun Fan said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang thought to himself: The average student really wouldn't be able to handle this. This thing really tests one's self-discipline.

"Teacher Xiong, how should we select our courses?"

A girl in the front row asked.

Teacher Xiong Wenxin said, "First, go attend your military training. After it's over, there will be a course selection planning meeting, where advisors will recommend course combinations based on students' interests. The advisors will also take turns giving lectures, explaining the general situation of various majors and courses, and the developmental history, popular trends, and cutting-edge achievements of major disciplines both at home and abroad."

"One advisor is also only responsible for 10 to 11 students. Once you decide, don't hesitate, or the advisor you like might already have a full quota of students. For the courses you choose, there is a two-week trial period. If you don't like a course, just find your advisor to sign off and re-select."

"Remember, popular courses have enrollment limits. If you're too slow, you won't get in. Also, you have to adjust your selected courses according to the class schedule, otherwise, you might have time conflicts."

After these words, the students below began to whisper and discuss among themselves.

Whether they were provincial top scorers, city top scorers, or winners of some first-place prize or gold medal, at this moment, their minds were all a complete blank.

Chen Guiliang was also a bit lost, with no idea how to choose his courses.

Teacher Xiong Wenxin said again, "Next, following the seating order from left to right, front to back, everyone please come up for a brief self-introduction. Let's welcome this student!"

The boy in the far-left seat of the front row ran up to the stage with a grin. "Hello everyone, my name is Lei Tuo. I'm from Liaodong, a science student. Lei as in thunder, Tuo as in to pioneer. My hobbies are playing Go and reading. Thank you!"

*Clap clap clap clap...*

The audience gave him a round of applause.

Immediately after, a girl went up. "Hello teacher, hello classmates. My name is Zou Shuya, from Lingnan, a liberal arts student. My hobbies are reading, listening to music, and watching movies..."

One student after another went on stage to introduce themselves.

Some were calm, some were nervous, but they were all quite confident. No one made a fool of themselves.

Everyone probably knew that the Yuanpei Program was full of hidden talents, so they all tacitly avoided mentioning past achievements, resolutely not talking about what they used to do. So what if you were second in your province or first in your city? There were a full 10 provincial top scorers in liberal arts and sciences here!

Chen Guiliang was in the second row, so his turn came quickly. "Hello everyone, my name is Chen Guiliang, from southern Sichuan..."

"Whoa~~~~"

"Hello, great talent!"

Before Chen Guiliang could even finish, at least 20 people started hooting. Nearly one-seventh of the entire class knew him.

The other students looked completely baffled, turning their heads to discuss with the classmates next to them.

"Who's Chen Guiliang?"

"Is he very famous? Has he been in a movie?"

"He can't be a sports star, can he?"

"He looks like a table tennis player."

"..."

Chen Guiliang raised his right index finger, held it in front of his lips, and said into the microphone, "Shhh~~~~"

After about half a minute of clamor, the classroom finally quieted down. Chen Guiliang continued, "Hello everyone, my name is Chen Guiliang, from southern Sichuan, a liberal arts student. I like making friends, shooting the bull, and playing video games."

"Clap clap clap clap!"

The applause this time was even more enthusiastic. Even those who didn't know him clapped their hands enthusiastically.

The more than 140 students weren't divided into classes, and their courses were all different.

Except for students with the same advisor and counselor, it would be difficult for other classmates to interact on a regular basis. It was possible that they might still not know each other even after graduating from university.

Chen Guiliang had a good start. On the very first day of introductions, he left an impression on the entire class.

After all the students had introduced themselves, Teacher Xiong Wenxin returned to the stage. "Now, let's elect the class committee. You can nominate yourselves. First, let's elect the class presidents, one for liberal arts and one for science, two main class presidents. Which student is willing to be a class president?"

"Chen Guiliang, Chen Guiliang for liberal arts class president!" several rascals shouted, trying to stir things up.

Chen Guiliang stood up with a smile and politely declined, "I'd rather not be the class president. All of you are brilliant people. I'm just someone who came out of a writing competition."

The main reason was that he didn't have the time.

Just thinking about being the class president of the Yuanpei Program sounded exhausting, especially since many students didn't have cell phones or computers yet!

The first class president of the first Yuanpei Program had it the worst. They didn't have third-year students as counselors, didn't attend classes together, and the whole class was scattered across nine different dormitory buildings. Very few people had cell phones back then. If the class president wanted to relay a message, they had to run from building to building, and even then, they might not find the person.

But someone wasn't afraid of the trouble.

A boy walked up to the podium. "Let me re-introduce myself. My name is Zhou Chu, the same name as the one who eliminated the three evils. I'm willing to serve as the liberal arts class president and serve all the students."

Teacher Xiong Wenxin asked, "Is there anyone else who wants to run for liberal arts class president?"

No one answered.

"Alright then. Now, will the liberal arts students please vote by raising your hands? If more than half of you raise your hands, it's passed."

A forest of hands shot up. He was passed unanimously!

Zhou Chu was very excited. He wrote down his cell phone number and said, "I just got this new SIM card today. If any of you need anything, you can call me."

Chen Guiliang took out his phone and saved the class president's number.

Next, the science class president, two vice presidents, the academic affairs officer, and a host of other class committee members were elected.

The teacher immediately slipped away, no longer concerned with their fate.

For the next few years, everything would rely on student autonomy.

The 14 third-year students moonlighting as counselors walked up to the podium, laughing and joking.

One of the counselors said, "Come and get your campus cards. The campus card was introduced two years ago. You can use it to pay for meals in the cafeteria and also as a library card. However, some cafeteria windows only accept cash. You'll need to deposit money onto the card, and it will be activated when you do."

"There's something like this? How convenient," Deng Chen marveled.

Chen Guiliang thought: As expected of Peking University. They had campus cards this early.

The senior counselors took turns speaking. "Tomorrow and the day after are the two days for the pre-military training physical exam. The training itself isn't held on campus. Your Yuanpei Program has been assigned to..."

There wasn't much to say about military training, just a general overview.

For the Peking University Class of '02, the military training was originally scheduled for the summer of '03. But then they ran into the SARS epidemic.

So, this year, the classes of '02, '03, and '04 from Peking University were all doing their military training at the same time!

The scale was enormous; a single base couldn't possibly hold everyone.

On the day Chen Guiliang went for his physical, all the sophomores and juniors had returned to campus. The three years of students, organized by department, charged full-steam ahead to Daxing, Huairou, and Yanqing.

Changping seemed to have been taken by Tsinghua; Tsinghua was also doing multiple years of training at once this year.

The Yuanpei Program trained together with the schools of Information Science, Chemistry, and Life Sciences. Other departments didn't come to this base.

During this time, a mess occurred.

From the third-year male students majoring in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, the drill instructors selected elite soldiers to form a hundred-man phalanx. They had extra practice every day on military boxing, and even added difficult moves like shoulder throws.

They trained so hard that almost everyone was injured. At the final drill performance, they stunned the entire audience.

And then, they got second place...

First place went to the female students from their same major.

"What's going on?" Jiang Junlai couldn't believe his ears.

Deng Chen, however, was a walking source of gossip. He whispered, "I heard that the 12th Company's drill instructor... needed some political achievement..."

Chen Guiliang stood silently in the formation, happy to just watch the show.

When the drill results were announced, not a single winning company went to the main platform.

"Down with XXXX!"

A slogan was suddenly shouted.

"Down with XXXX!"

"XXXX is corrupt!"

"..."

People flocked to join in, and the slogans grew more and more outrageous, the kind that would get you 404'd if written out.

Yun Fan murmured to himself, "Is this Peking University?"

Jiang Junlai said, "A real eye-opener."

Deng Chen said, "The senior students are so badass!"

Chen Guiliang watched, greatly amused.

The aftermath was a complete mess.

The students from the involved company were fine. In fact, they hardly trained at all after that, and were even treated to better food. No one cared if they played cards in their dorms all day.

But their drill instructors seemed incredibly aggrieved. At the end of the training, they got dead drunk with the students.

After this incident, Peking University's military training never came to this base again.
